newsitem.title: UK: UK venture capital applauds some Budget changes.
newsitem.headline: UK venture capital applauds some Budget changes.

text.p: The British Venture Capital Association has welcomed some changes made by the Chancellor in the Budget but added that others, such as cutting capital gains tax, were vital to encourage an "enterprise culture" in the UK.
A statement from the BVCA said the Budget had made some moves towards assisting small firms, which account for two thirds of employment and 58 percent of the UK private sector turnover.
"But what would have been of the most significance to these companies -- a cut in the rate of Capital Gains Tax -- has only been promised."
The association said Britain has the highest marginal rate of CGT among its competitor countries and easing it would "result in little or no losses to the Exchequer".

It said relaxation of the rules covering Venture Capital Trusts (VCTs) and the Enterprise Investment Scheme were welcome, and would allow the 12 VCTs which have raised a total 163 million stg to extend their lives and draw in more investors.
Although corporation tax for small companies had been reduced from 24 percent to 23 percent, the BVCA said it would continue to lobby for 20 percent.
It also wants the threshold for tax to be raised to 500,000 stg from 300,000 stg with the marginal rate applying up to 2.5 million stg, to encourage further earnings retention.
